quote: Parts of the materiel notified by Belarus have not only been diverted upon arrival at Tripoli International Airport by brigades controlling it
notes: Ammunition imported by the Libyan Ministry of Defence (notified, Belarus) taken by Zintan brigades. Belarus not coded: deliveries by private carriers.

quote: Since the outbreak of the conflict in 2014, the Sudan has been transferring military materiel to Libya in violation of the arms embargo.
notes: Evidence type to confirm from paragraph context.

quote: The Panel has investigated additional transfers from the United Arab Emirates in violation of the arms embargo.
notes: Streit APCs approved for export to Tripoli without notification; Nimr APCs and AR-M9F rifles to the Sawa'iq brigade (annex 27).

quote: the Sudan has continued to transfer materiel to Libya in violation of the arms embargo
notes: Based on two Member States and armed-group representatives (p34) and Chinese ammunition in Sudanese packaging documented by CAR in Sabha (p37: 'may have retransferred').

quote: The ammunition was transferred from Pakistan to Qatar, which re-transferred it to Libya in 2011 in violation of the arms embargo
notes: Restates S/2013/99 paras 67 ff. Pakistan is the manufacturer, not coded.

quote: the Panel finds that the United Arab Emirates is in non-compliance with paragraph 9 of resolution 1970 (2011) for the post-delivery transfer of this ammunition to Libya.
notes: Also Wing Loong II UCAV with Blue Arrow missiles (p34, annex table 28.1).

quote: finds that they did transfer military materiel, and therefore that Turkey, ProAir-Charter-Transport GmbH and the carriers' agent Plures Air Cargo were all in non-compliance
notes: Bayraktar TB2 UCAVs (table 27.1).

quote: The Panel finds that Turkey is in non-compliance with paragraph 9 of resolution 1970 (2011) for the transfer of military materiel to Libya.
Transfer of Akinci UCAV to Libya is a violation of paragraph 9 of resolution 1970 (2011) by Türkiye.
notes: Training findings in the same report are excluded (protocol section 3).

quote: Jordan, Turkey and the United Arab Emirates routinely and sometimes blatantly supplied weapons, employing little effort to disguise the source.
notes: From the report summary; the equipment detail is in the body and annexes, still to read.

quote: The stockpile of SCUD-B and SCUD-C variant (HWASONG-6) SRBM captured by the Houthi around Sana'a was relatively small.
notes: Report first circulated as S/2017/81. Yemeni state missile stocks taken by Houthi forces; evidence type to confirm from annexes.

quote: with serial numbers consistent with the batches of those operated by the GoY, presented for sale in Houthi-controlled areas
notes: Type 56-1 rifles; China is the manufacturer, not coded.

quote: The Panel has, however, confirmed that SPLM/A in Opposition has received ammunition and, to a lesser extent, arms, as well as other items such as uniforms, from the Sudan.
notes: Supply to an armed opposition group.

quote: the weapons were transferred to the National Security Service in 2014. According to the Government of Israel, Uganda did not request permission for the transfer.
notes: Israeli Micro Galil rifles sold to Uganda's Ministry of Defence in 2007; re-transfer without the exporter's consent (before the 2018 UN embargo, so the breach is of the end-user undertaking).

quote: the Sudan has provided small arms, ammunition and some logistical support to the Sudan People's Liberation Movement/Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLM/A) in Opposition
notes: Restates and extends S/2016/70.

quote: There is no provision in the end user certificate for their transfer to South Sudan.
notes: Three more rifles from the same 2007 batch; 'supports the conclusion that they are part of a larger group of weapons transferred from Uganda'.

quote: Lieutenant General Kuc, violated the embargo on arms by obtaining three deliveries of weapons, mostly AK-47s, and related ammunition from the National Intelligence and Security Service of the Sudan
notes: After the 2018 UN embargo on all of South Sudan.

quote: The Panel confirmed the use of the Rakhsh armoured personnel carrier in Darfur; a certain violation of the arms embargo by the Government of the Sudan.
notes: The Government moving its own materiel to its forces in Darfur without the exemption the embargo requires; counts under protocol section 3 ('any user in an embargoed territory without the required exemption'). Can be separated in sensitivity analysis. Also S-8DM rockets (p19).

quote: The Government of the Sudan continues to transfer military material to Darfur in support of the various security forces deployed there and in violation of the arms embargo.
notes: The Government moving its own materiel to its forces in Darfur without the exemption the embargo requires; counts under protocol section 3 ('any user in an embargoed territory without the required exemption'). Can be separated in sensitivity analysis.

quote: During the reporting period, the Government of the Sudan continued to transfer arms and other military material into Darfur in violation of the arms embargo.
notes: The Government moving its own materiel to its forces in Darfur without the exemption the embargo requires; counts under protocol section 3 ('any user in an embargoed territory without the required exemption'). Can be separated in sensitivity analysis.

quote: According to information gathered by the Panel from sources in Chad and Darfur, the allegations were credible.
notes: Allegations that the UAE gave military support to RSF through Am Djarass airport, Chad (weapons and ammunition unloaded from cargo planes several times a week, per several sources). The Panel judges them credible but makes no formal finding: CLOSE CALL, check in second coding.

quote: the Panel confirmed that KOMID had provided key components to the Oamites munitions factory
notes: KOMID is the DPRK's main state arms trader. Same report: small arms shipped from the DPRK to the DRC Presidential Guard and police (para 104, from the DRC Group of Experts). Breach of the embargo on DPRK arms exports.

quote: in 2014 the Group also identified that Congolese soldiers gave arms and ammunition to several armed groups, including FDLR, RUD and Mai Mai Yakutumba
notes: Detail in paras 71 and 115 (ex-combatant and armed-group testimony). Also a stockpile-safety finding at Goma (annex 43).

quote: A senior FARDC officer ... told the Group that on numerous occasions he had arrested troops under his command for selling or giving weapons, ammunition and/or uniforms to FRPI.
notes: Corroborated by another senior officer and two FARDC judges, but the Group states no finding; coded probable. S/2016/466 para 229 cites this paragraph as 'previously reported'. Close call for second coding.

quote: some individuals within FARDC continue to divert materiel for sale on the black market and to armed groups.
notes: Summary (p3): 'the Group found that armed groups continued to benefit from leakage from government stocks'. Military court cases on thefts from the Goma logistics base (annex 63). Also para 200: an FARDC colonel supplied ADF with ammunition (testimony).

quote: the Panel traced back to the Democratic Republic of the Congo eight Galil assault rifles seized from armed groups, including the former Séléka and LRA.
notes: How the rifles left Congolese control is not stated; details in annex 9.33, which is not in the public report. Same paragraph: former Séléka 'reportedly' source arms in the DRC (not a finding).

quote: Israel informed the Panel that three additional Galil assault rifles ... seized in the CAR were sold to the government of the Republic of Chad in 2008 and 2009.
notes: Manufacturer Israel (IWI). Sold under an end-user certificate barring transfer to another country. Chad told the Panel the rifles had been issued to its embassy security in the CAR, its security detail for Bozizé and its MISCA troops: how they reached armed groups is not established, so unclear. Two earlier rifles traced in S/2014/762 (outside the window).

quote: it is highly likely that they come from the same source
notes: Type 56-2 rifles from Al-Shabaab's Mogadishu airport attack, matched visually to the Ethiopian 2013 delivery to the FGS whose rifles the 2014 report traced from SNA stockpiles to Mogadishu markets. Manufacturer: Chinese pattern; supplier Ethiopia not coded (delivery to the government). Para 18: SNA personnel 'asserted' to supply Bakara market (not a finding).

quote: The Group received consistent testimony that diversions from national stocks continued to be the main source of supply for armed groups in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
notes: FARDC officers say most documented arms 'might have been' transferred from national stocks; para 160: Mai Mai Kilalo casings with head stamps similar to national stocks (annex 52). Coded probable.

quote: While the Group continues to investigate how FRPI obtained the ammunition, it notes the high likelihood of this representing a violation of the arms embargo.
notes: Head stamp LI-02, Luwero Industries (Uganda) 2002; Uganda told the Group the ammunition is for local use only, so it came from Ugandan holdings. How it left them is not established.

quote: the SEMG again documented cases of weapons from FGS stockpiles found in possession of individuals or illicit arms dealers in Mogadishu.
notes: Seven weapons with Somali Police Force, NISA and FGS-issued private security markings at Bakara market and KM5; seven more FGS-marked rifles seized from individuals in the June 2017 stabilization operation (para 5).

quote: The Group consulted the military court registry and identified 13 cases related to the sales of weapons and ammunition by national security forces to armed groups
notes: Also the Mai-Mai Yakutumba looting of the FARDC armoury at Bendera, 1 June 2017 (para 95), and a police officer's sale of an AK-47 to Nyatura Domi on an FARDC colonel's instruction (para 99).

quote: armed groups continued to obtain materiel from the national stock of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, either through targeted attacks on FARDC depots or through the sale
notes: Para 184: FARDC officers say an improvised recoilless rifle ('solola bien') recovered from Mai-Mai Yakutumba was diverted from FARDC stock.

quote: two FDN sources with access to information confirmed to the Group that some government officials remained involved in the cross-border activities of armed individuals and the transfer of arms
notes: Burundian army officers and Imbonerakure members describe 33 AK-47s, 4 PKMs and grenades sent across the Ruzizi in Nov 2017; couriers said they were 'on mission for authorities from Burundi'. Burundi denied it (S/2017/1091 para 93). Testimony only and no formal finding against the Government: probable. Close call for second coding.

quote: Of the 48 weapons, 37 could be traced to the consignment of AK-pattern assault rifles of mid-2017. Thirteen of the documented weapons had been distributed to soldiers in sector 60
notes: Weapons with markings of FGS imports in arms dealers' hands. Also para 35 (FGS-headstamped rounds seized from Al-Shabaab) and para 49 (FGS-marked rifles in a UPDF seizure from Al-Shabaab).

quote: the plate was among a lot of 432 sold to the Ministry of Defence and Aviation of Saudi Arabia on 14 October 2001.
notes: Belgian (Mecar) hand grenade seized from Al-Shabaab by the UPDF. Para 57: Bulgarian 2013 ammunition in a Puntland seizure was sold to the UAE and Saudi Arabia in 2015 (which of the two not established). Saudi Arabia did not reply (para 58).

quote: The Group also received confirmation that two RPG-7 rounds manufactured in Bulgaria had been sold to the Ministry of Defence of Yemen in 2005.
notes: Seized from Al-Shabaab. How they left Yemeni state stocks is not stated.

quote: Other equipment documented in the seizure had likely been captured by Al-Shabaab following previous attacks on AMISOM forces.
notes: Example given: an FFV 651 Carl Gustav round, made in India, supplied to Kenya in June 2008. Kenya contributes AMISOM troops. 'Likely' captured: probable.

quote: sold to Yugoimport SDPR for onward delivery to Abu Dhabi in May 2016, with the Armed Forces of the United Arab Emirates listed as the end user.
notes: Two M-84s (Zastava, Serbia) in the September 2017 Puntland seizure of arms smuggled from Yemen. Bulgarian ammunition in the same seizure sold to the UAE and Saudi Arabia (para 57). The UAE did not answer how they reached the illicit market (para 58). End-user certificates barred re-export without Bulgarian permission.

quote: the light machine gun had been exported with an end-user certificate dated 30 November 2009 for sole use by the United States Army.
notes: Romanian PKM in a consignment from Yemen found with a Bosaso arms dealer. The ammunition lot went to a private US importer (not coded). The US did not answer how the materiel was diverted in Yemen (para 61).

quote: MONUSCO and FARDC sources and one local authority confirmed that the assailants had seized weapons and ammunition from the FARDC camp.
notes: ADF attack on the FARDC position at Ngadi, 24 August 2018: 17 AK-type rifles, two 60 mm mortars, 7 PK machine guns and a B10 recoilless rifle taken (one MONUSCO source).

theatre: DR Congo (Maniema, North and South Kivu)
quote: Armed groups continued to target FARDC camps and weapons depots in order to seize weapons and ammunition
notes: Looting of the FARDC position at Namoya, 24 May 2018, after a tip from an FARDC contact (paras 198-199); also para 43 (ADF).

quote: The delivery of weapons and ammunition to armed groups active in the Democratic Republic of the Congo ... as in this case, constitute violations of the arms embargo.
notes: Four Mai-Mai Kijangala combatants said the Burundian army (FDN) gave them weapons, ammunition and food when it left Congolese territory (para 194); the Group concludes in para 196. Testimony only: close call for second coding.

quote: the authorities of Burundi confirmed that the cartridges documented were part of the materiel with which renegade soldiers involved in the failed coup d'état of 2015 had fled.
notes: Burundi's own account; the Group could not match the markings to the inventory Burundi supplied, so probable. Combatants said FDN fired the same cartridges (para 194).

quote: Still images and video footage ... appear to confirm that militants captured weapons, ammunition and vehicles.
notes: Al-Shabaab attack on a Kenyan Defence Forces base, 27 January 2017: a 105 mm howitzer, a WZ-551 APC, an 81 mm mortar and an M240B machine gun. 'Appear to confirm': probable. Added on 26 Nov after re-reading for the S/2019/858 mortar trace.

quote: The mortar had likely been captured during the Al-Shabaab attack on the AMISOM Burundian contingent at Leego.
notes: 120 mm mortar used against the Baledogle base, 23 April 2017.

quote: Testimonies received from three arms dealers in Mogadishu confirmed that weapons bearing Federal Government markings had been purchased mostly from low-ranking members of the Somali security forces
notes: 38 FGS-marked weapons with arms dealers, some traced by serial to deliveries of 2014 and 2017. Annex 2.6: a pistol from the UAE's 2014 delivery to the FGS used in an Al-Shabaab killing (UAE not coded: delivered to the government).

quote: Kenya is the only troop contributing country in AMISOM equipped with 81-mm mortars.
notes: 81 mm mortar rounds (UK-made, 1975-76) in three Al-Shabaab attacks on Mogadishu; linked to the capture of 81 mm mortars at the Kulbiyow KDF base (S/2017/924 para 20). Inference, and Kenya did not reply: probable.

quote: photographs released by Al-Shabaab ... revealed that the group had captured a significant quantity of military equipment in El Adde, including armoured personnel carriers and self-propelled guns
notes: Al-Shabaab overran the Kenyan AMISOM base at El Adde, 15 January 2016 (paras 15-17, annex 1.1). Evidence is Al-Shabaab's own photographs as analysed by the Group.

quote: The Group found that transfer of materiel from FARDC members to NDC-R has continued
notes: Authenticated videos and 14 NDC-R combatants: ammunition handed over by FARDC members, joint FARDC-NDC-R operations against APCLS, two 82 mm mortars and a 12.7 mm machine gun delivered to NDC-R (para 73). Whether units acted on their own or as policy is not established, so unclear rather than leakage or re-transfer. Close call for second coding.

case_id: Sudanese stockpiles and regional weapon diversion: captured equipment held by SPLA-North in the Nuba Mountains-SDN-re-transfer
report: Sudanese stockpiles and regional weapon diversion: captured equipment held by SPLA-North in the Nuba Mountains
quote: Sudan's domestic production capacity has also expanded ... allowing it to ... supply its own materiel to non-state armed groups
notes: Mortar rounds of recent Sudanese manufacture with non-state groups in South Sudan and Côte d'Ivoire (pp46-48); Chinese 12.7 mm ammunition imported by Sudan's NISS captured from SPLA-iO in Unity state (pp49-50). CAR says repackaging conceals re-transfer in breach of end-user agreements with China. Manufacturer China not coded.

case_id: Weapon supplies into South Sudan's civil war: regional re-transfers and international intermediaries-UGA-re-transfer
report: Weapon supplies into South Sudan's civil war: regional re-transfers and international intermediaries
theatre: South Sudan; Sudan (Blue Nile, South Kordofan)
quote: SOME OF THE MILITARY MATERIEL RETRANSFERRED TO SOUTH SUDAN WAS EXPORTED BY STATES THAT HAD ALREADY IMPOSED PROHIBITIONS ON ARMS SUPPLIES
notes: Bulgarian rifles and ammunition bought for the Ugandan MOD (2014-15) match ammunition with the SPLA and its Sudanese allies; SPLA correspondence to the UPDF on the procurement names the Ugandan importer (pp48-50). For Romanian ammunition CAR 'has not determined the means of diversion' (p51). Aircraft supplied through a private Ugandan-US company network (pp54-62), not coded to Uganda. Mechanism inferred from documents, not stated as a Ugandan government decision: probable. Close call for second coding.

quote: Some of the materiel delivered to FARDC was later diverted to armed groups in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.
notes: Para 13: CMC/FDP bought ammunition from FARDC members. Annex 78 lists Chinese-pattern materiel delivered to FARDC and later found with armed groups.

quote: The Panel confirmed that on 22 April, the vehicle, weapons and ammunition were no longer at the FACA camp.
notes: Weapons seized from FPRC and held at the FACA camp in Birao went missing; local sources say they were sold to MLCJ and Kara youth. FACA commanders say they went to Bangui, but no record was found. Loss confirmed, sale reported: probable.

quote: The weapon, which bears apparent Federal Government markings, was distributed to the Somali National Army in sector 60, in Baidoa, South-West State
notes: Assault rifle used in Al-Shabaab's Manda Bay attack (Kenya, 28 Dec 2019) traced to a July 2017 delivery to the FGS. Para 98-99 area: two rifles previously delivered to the FGS among 33 captured from Al-Shabaab by AMISOM (p26).

case_id: Dispatch: Weapons and ammunition airdropped to SPLA-iO forces in South Sudan-SDN-re-transfer
report: Dispatch: Weapons and ammunition airdropped to SPLA-iO forces in South Sudan
quote: The recent date of manufacture is further evidence of direct supply from Khartoum to SPLA-iO forces.
notes: Airdrop-damaged ammunition captured from SPLA-iO in Pigi County, Nov 2014: 70% of 7.62 x 39 mm rounds Sudanese-made, mostly 2014; Type 56-1 serials in sequence with Sudan's 2011 supplies to South Sudanese rebels. CAR says the evidence 'suggests' direct supply: probable.

case_id: Non-state armed groups in the Central African Republic: types and sources of documented arms and ammunition-SDN-re-transfer
report: Non-state armed groups in the Central African Republic: types and sources of documented arms and ammunition
quote: Chinese- and possible Iranian-manufactured small arms ammunition and larger munitions have been re-transferred from Sudan to CAR.
notes: 2013 Sudanese ammunition in former Séléka stockpiles 'supporting well-documented reports of arms supplies from Sudan'; Sudanese-made light tactical vehicles. The report shows the route through Sudan but not who in Sudan passed it on: probable.

case_id: Non-state armed groups in the Central African Republic: types and sources of documented arms and ammunition-CAF-leakage
report: Non-state armed groups in the Central African Republic: types and sources of documented arms and ammunition
quote: Séléka appears to have seized much of its weaponry from Bozizé-era stockpiles, which have also leaked to armed civilians on all sides.
notes: Seizure of government stockpiles during and after Séléka's 2013 takeover. 'Appears': probable.

quote: The Group documented instances of weapons and ammunition being transferred from certain FARDC officers to NDC-R
notes: Over 20 testimonies: General Gahizi, deputy commander of the 34th military region, instructed FARDC units to supply NDC-R since 2018 (para 34); weapons moved in FARDC vehicles; Bwira faction took arms from the FARDC position in Pinga (para 33). Regional command involvement, but not established as government policy: unclear, as for S/2019/974. Close call for second coding.

quote: on 23 December, 3R and anti-balaka CPC forces seized one of the donated BRDM-2 armoured vehicles following fighting with government forces in Boali
notes: BRDM-2 donated by Russia in October 2020; confirmed by government sources. Annex 6: USMS elements seized weapons from their camp armoury in Bouar and deserted with arms (p138, partly 'reported').

theatre: DR Congo (Ituri, South Kivu Hauts-Plateaux, Beni)
quote: Most of the CODECO factions' military materiel came from attacks on FARDC bases and soldiers.
notes: Para 92: 105 AK-type rifles, 5 PKMs, 3 RPG-7s, a mortar and a 107 mm launcher looted at Ritsi, 8 May 2020. Para 143: diversion of FARDC weaponry to Mai-Mai and Twirwaneho; 46 FARDC members arrested for trafficking. Paras 40-43: FARDC units selling ammunition to Garamba park guards.

case_id: Investigating cross-border weapon transfers in the Sahel-LBY-leakage
report: Investigating cross-border weapon transfers in the Sahel
theatre: Mali; Central African Republic; Lebanon; Syria; Côte d'Ivoire
quote: CAR documented weapons in six countries throughout Africa and the Middle East that either certainly, or very probably, originated in Libyan stockpiles.
notes: SA-7b MANPADS, F7 rockets, M79 rockets, Polish rifles (Poland confirmed exports to Libya among five states) and mortar rounds matching Sebha stocks. The 2011 collapse released the national stockpile from government control (p6).

case_id: Investigating cross-border weapon transfers in the Sahel-MLI-leakage
report: Investigating cross-border weapon transfers in the Sahel
quote: Malian armed movements have employed an increasing proportion of heavy weaponry from Malian government stockpiles
notes: One 122 mm rocket traced to Malian state stocks through its exporter; lot numbers of many more match abandoned FAMa stores near Gao (at least 20% of the sample).

case_id: Investigating cross-border weapon transfers in the Sahel-CIV-leakage
report: Investigating cross-border weapon transfers in the Sahel
theatre: Mali; Côte d'Ivoire; Central African Republic
quote: their original diversion from Ivorian state stockpiles may have occurred several years ago.
notes: Chinese rifles exported to Ivorian forces found with armed groups in Mali (2015) and the CAR; ammunition 'of likely Ivorian state provenance' used against Malian forces. Point of diversion uncertain: probable.

case_id: Investigating cross-border weapon transfers in the Sahel-IRQ-unclear
report: Investigating cross-border weapon transfers in the Sahel
quote: their correspondence with weapons of Iraqi manufacture or originally in Iraqi state stocks ... further suggests that they may not be from the Sahel region.
notes: E.g. a Hungarian AK63 with an Iraqi import mark used at Tenenkou, January 2015. Iraqi state origin suggested, route unknown: unclear, probable.

quote: Each of the three groups was provided with weapons, gendarmerie uniforms and one gendarmerie vehicle.
notes: PK5 self-defence fighters recruited 'under the direct supervision of the Minister of the Interior' through a parallel process outside the formal forces (para 108); eyewitnesses and photographs. Whether co-opted militias count as unauthorised users is a judgement: probable, close call for second coding. Vehicle is a gendarmerie vehicle, not armoured as such.

quote: a 60mm mortar round, with characteristics consistent with 60mm M73 HE manufactured in 2016 in Serbia and exported the same year to Saudi Arabia.
notes: Same type fired by Al-Shabaab at the UN compound, 17 Feb 2020. The Panel asked Saudi Arabia where in its chain of custody it was diverted (fn 102). 'Consistent with': probable.

quote: The Panel also identified military equipment previously delivered to the Federal Government of Somalia (type 56-2 and armoured personnel carrier).
notes: Identified in Al-Shabaab material (attacks and released videos, annex).

quote: one pistol and 12 assault rifles have serial numbers matching, or very similar to, those delivered to the Federal Government of Somalia
notes: About 20% of the weapons AMISOM/ATMIS captured from Al-Shabaab; three with NISA and two with SNA markings. Heading: 'captured or diverted from Somali security forces'.

quote: The Group found substantial evidence attesting to violations of the arms embargo and sanctions regime, including ... (b) provision of weapons, ammunition and uniforms to M23/ARC
notes: In the context of RDF incursions and operations with M23/ARC (paras 47-51); drone imagery of cross-border supply of artillery, weapons and ammunition (para 46); new uniforms, helmets and vests (para 44). Rwanda denied support (para 51).

quote: members of the coalition of armed groups received weapons and ammunition from FARDC members on several occasions
notes: After the Pinga meeting, CMC/FDP, APCLS, FDLR, NDC-R and MPA fought alongside FARDC against M23/ARC. Summary: 'support to several Congolese armed groups by FARDC members' and 'cooperation between FARDC units and Congolese armed groups'. Whether this was government policy is not established here: unclear, close call for second coding.

quote: the objective of the RDF military actions ... was to reinforce M23 by providing troops and materiel
notes: Sources include two RDF intelligence personnel. Summary: 'further evidence of direct interventions by the Rwanda Defence Force', recent M23 equipment 'attested to violations of the arms embargo'. Coded consistently with S/2022/967.

quote: at the instruction of Generals Mayanga and Mugabo, FARDC provided armed groups with uniforms, weapons, ammunition, generators, fuel, food and monetary incentives.
notes: Summary: collaboration with the ARP coalition, including the sanctioned FDLR, 'was coordinated by senior FARDC officers'; the second-in-command of operations against M23 convened meetings 'between the official military hierarchy and armed group leaders' (para 80). Unlike earlier reports, this is directed by the command: re-transfer. Close call for second coding.

case_id: Weapons of the Islamic State: a three-year investigation in Iraq and Syria-USA-re-transfer
report: Weapons of the Islamic State: a three-year investigation in Iraq and Syria
quote: The United States and Saudi Arabia supplied most of this materiel without authorisation, apparently to Syrian opposition forces.
notes: Warsaw Pact-calibre materiel bought from EU states in Eastern Europe and re-transferred without the exporters' consent, then recovered from IS; fastest case an EU-made ATGW sold to the US. CAR calls unauthorised retransfer 'a significant source of IS weapons'.

case_id: Weapons of the Islamic State: a three-year investigation in Iraq and Syria-SAU-re-transfer
report: Weapons of the Islamic State: a three-year investigation in Iraq and Syria
quote: The United States and Saudi Arabia supplied most of this materiel without authorisation, apparently to Syrian opposition forces.
notes: As for the United States row: purchases from EU Member States re-transferred into the Syrian conflict in breach of non-retransfer undertakings; recovered from IS forces.

case_id: Weapons of the Islamic State: a three-year investigation in Iraq and Syria-IRQ-leakage
report: Weapons of the Islamic State: a three-year investigation in Iraq and Syria
quote: These findings support widespread assumptions that the group initially captured much of its military materiel from Iraqi and Syrian government forces.
notes: Battlefield capture; CAR frames it as supporting assumptions rather than tracing each item: probable.

case_id: Weapons of the Islamic State: a three-year investigation in Iraq and Syria-SYR-leakage
report: Weapons of the Islamic State: a three-year investigation in Iraq and Syria
quote: These findings support widespread assumptions that the group initially captured much of its military materiel from Iraqi and Syrian government forces.
notes: Russian-made weapons outnumber Chinese among IS forces in Syria, 'presumably reflecting Russian supplies to the Syrian regime'. Probable.

quote: Diversion from police stockpiles – through theft or loss – has resulted in police weapons and ammunition regularly ending up in the hands of criminals and gang members
notes: Section 2.3.1 and annex 33; seized firearms also mismanaged and diverted (annex 34).

quote: The Panel identified that these boxes were part of ammunition delivered to Somalia in February 2022 for Danab special forces
notes: Bulgarian ammunition boxes among materiel captured from Al-Shabaab and inspected at Halane; annex 11 table lists captured rifles, some with SNA markings.

quote: The FARDC provided arms, logistics and cash to VDP leaders and combatants ... in violation of the arms embargo and sanctions regime.
notes: Coordinated by FARDC colonels, with the North Kivu Governor's office coordinating VDP operations (para 39); annex 25 and appendix on weaponry provided to armed groups fighting M23.

quote: The Mobondo have become more organized and gradually increased their military capabilities by attacking FARDC and police elements, stealing weapons and ammunition.
notes: Battlefield capture and theft from security forces.
